paras: The threatened lynching of Jesse James took place in August 1910 near Leola, Grant County, Arkansas, when a mob gathered to capture James, a Black man accused of attempting to assault a fourteen-year-old girl. City Marshal Charles Stephens arrested him and took him by way of Pine Bluff to the county jail at Sheridan, and the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic reported that he would otherwise have been lynched.

According to the girl, Sarah Children, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. J. M. Children, James made an "insulting remark" to her when she went to his home, near her own, on an errand for her mother. She said that when he tried to get her to come to him she ran home, and that James, about thirty-five years old, pursued her two hundred yards.

When James learned that a mob was gathering to capture him, he fled the neighborhood. Marshal Stephens arrested him on Sunday, 14 August, and the next day brought him through Pine Bluff, where James spent several hours in the county jail between trains. From there the marshal took him to Sheridan, the Grant County seat, to be held "for safe keeping."
James denied the charge of attempted criminal assault and said the girl had been "frightened without cause." No report of an indictment, trial or later outcome appears in the coverage.

The only report found is a front-page item in the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic of 16 August 1910, headlined "NEGRO HURRIED AWAY FROM MOB." The paper called James "a negro with a famous name," described the charge as an "alleged crime," and printed his denial alongside the girl's account, without comment on the mob. No other white paper and no Black paper was found carrying the story.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of Jesse James (Leola, Arkansas)
bases: A1 reports that a mob gathered to capture Jesse James after he was accused of attempted criminal assault and states that he 'would have been lynched' had the marshal not hurried him away; no one was harmed, so the episode is a threatened lynching.

No one was killed: A1 reports only that a mob was gathering to capture James and that he was taken to jail for safe keeping, so the episode is a threatened lynching, not a lynching; the mob's size is not given.
The only report found is the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic (A1); no other white or Black paper was found carrying the episode.
